tweets: Price oracle manipulation exploits vulnerabilities in price feeds to alter contract logic.
This can lead to unauthorized actions, fund loss, or exploitation of the contract's core logic.
A primary remediation is leveraging multiple decentralized oracles for price data.
Validating all incoming oracle inputs before use prevents many manipulation vectors.
Aggregating data from several DEXs or oracles using median or mean values helps resist attacks.
Rejecting outliers and anomalous deviations further strengthens the aggregated price feed.
Time-based defenses like TWAPs over sufficient windows resist short-lived price manipulations.
Prices older than a maximum staleness threshold should be rejected to ensure freshness.
Liquidity-aware design avoids basing core prices on illiquid pools that are easily manipulated.
Capping the impact of a single pool or feed on global pricing limits individual failure.
